events.credibility_reason: An asymptotic Lemoine theorem would be a landmark well beyond Chen-type results. There has been no expert uptake in nearly six years. The same authors' related preprint conceded that a key lemma was wrong, and the method (circles of partition) is elementary and sits outside the mainstream sieve and circle-method approaches.
The author's own v6 comment concedes that the Little Lemma proof was wrong and the proof is conditional. The full-conjecture claim was dropped in v9 (Nov 2023), and Wikipedia records it as flawed.

Same signals as the 2020 asymptotic claim: a landmark-level asymptotic result with no uptake in four years, from an author whose related full-conjecture claim rested on a lemma they conceded was wrong, using a method the field has not adopted.
This is a claimed binary Goldbach result with no uptake, and it concerns a different problem.

It is labelled 'machine-verified', but the Lean files declare no theorem, only a search function, so the correctness claim, which is the conjecture itself, is never stated or proved. Its central modular identity is asserted, not derived. There has been no engagement, the author is anonymous and outside the field, and the claim would be a landmark.

events.ai_basis: Claude Opus 4.8 resolved 30% of the 492 conjectures. (Row-level attribution to this model comes from the results repository's info.json for oeis_236566_conjecture_2.)

Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol were evaluated only on Lite, and only with the base agent. (Row-level attribution to this model comes from the results repository's info.json for oeis_219055_conjecture_1.)

why: Both OEIS Open rows prove only implications: each derives Lemoine from an open Sun conjecture. That is a reduction to an unproven condition, so the scope is none even though the Lean conclusion is Lemoine's statement. The models did produce those implication proofs, so ai_role is generated per row; the rows are discarded on scope, not on AI role. The AEjonanonymous repository claims the whole conjecture, but its Lean files state no theorem, and several other F10 signals are present, so it is not_credible. Among the pre-snapshot events, the Agama–Gensel full claim was conceded conditional by the author, so it is knocked_down. Their asymptotic claims are cases (sufficiently large n), and I set them aside as not_credible on F10 signals. That is a close call against doubtful, but they predate the snapshot and are case-scope, so they cannot produce open_stale either way. Juhász et al. is a finite check up to 10^13.
doubts: The model attribution for both OEIS rows rests on the results repository's per-sample info.json rather than on the paper's prose. The paper itself warns that some formalisations are likely misformalized. Neither point changes the scope answer. The asymptotic Agama–Gensel claims were judged from abstracts only.
